sports.label: NHL

brain.approach: Score- and opponent-adjusted 5v5 expected-goals ratings, special-teams xG and penalty rates, goalie goals-saved-above-expected, rest and back-to-backs → a Poisson regression for each team's regulation goals → an exact score distribution with empirical score effects and goalie-pull dynamics, 3-on-3 overtime and the shootout → every market's fair price.
brain.why: Hockey is low-scoring and noisy: goals are a weak signal, shot quality (xG) is a stronger and more stable one (macdonald2012). Leaders sit back and trailing teams pull the goalie, so margins and totals are not plain Poisson (tulsky2012, beaudoin2010). A full distribution, not a single number, is what the moneyline, the puck line and the total all need.

sports.label: MLB

brain.approach: Existing: a negative-binomial run model on probable starters and offense features. Designed upgrade: starter quality from xERA/FIP/K-BB% with times-through-order decay, bullpen availability from the last three days' pitch counts, lineup wOBA with platoon splits, park and weather run factors → a run distribution per team → moneyline, run line, total.
brain.why: The starter is the largest single input but pitches ~5 innings; bullpen usage and platoon matchups decide the rest (tango2007). Runs are overdispersed, so a negative binomial beats Poisson.

sports.label: College baseball

brain.approach: Designed: opponent-adjusted run ratings (a ridge-regularised attack/defence run model, as for soccer goals) with weekend-rotation starters and park effects.
brain.why: Hundreds of teams with few common opponents: shrinkage and opponent adjustment matter more than pitch-level detail, which is not available.

blockers: No validated model (lib/college_baseball.js refuses to publish a projection).
enable: Build the run-ratings brain and validate it walk-forward; then authorise price capture.

sports.label: NBA

brain.approach: Designed: opponent-adjusted offensive/defensive efficiency per 100 possessions and pace, adjusted for lineup availability through regularised player impact (RAPM), → a normal margin and total around possession-based projections.
brain.why: Possessions normalise pace (kubatko2007); margins are close to Brownian/normal (stern1994); star availability moves lines by points, so player impact must be priced (sill2010).

blockers: No schedule, box-score, play-by-play or availability source is wired; prices are not captured.
enable: Wire a play-by-play source (e.g. the NBA stats endpoints via a public mirror such as sportsdataverse hoopR data), build ratings and RAPM, validate walk-forward, then authorise capture.

sports.label: WNBA

brain.approach: Designed: the NBA brain with WNBA priors (fewer games, larger roster turnover, heavier shrinkage).
brain.why: Same game structure (kubatko2007, stern1994); smaller samples need stronger regularisation.

blockers: No data wired; prices not captured.
enable: As for the NBA, with sportsdataverse wehoop data.

sports.label: Men's college basketball

brain.approach: Designed: opponent-adjusted efficiency and tempo solved by ridge regression over the season's possessions, with home court and travel.
brain.why: 360+ teams and sparse schedules: opponent adjustment by regularised least squares is the published standard (kubatko2007).

blockers: No ingest in this repository (the deployed-only ingest_multisport is outside it); prices not captured.
enable: Wire sportsdataverse hoopR men's college data, build the brain, validate, then authorise capture.

sports.label: Women's college basketball

brain.approach: Designed: as men's, with women's priors.
brain.why: Same structure; thinner markets and data.

blockers: No data wired; no price source wired.
enable: Wire sportsdataverse wehoop women's college data; build and validate.

sports.label: Soccer

brain.approach: Designed: time-weighted attack/defence Poisson with the Dixon-Coles low-score correction, xG-informed ratings where shot data exist, home advantage per league, lineup availability; three-way and Asian-handicap settlement.
brain.why: The Dixon-Coles model is the published, market-tested baseline for football scores (dixoncoles1997, maher1982); Elo is a strong simple baseline (hvattum2010); correlated scores need care (karlis2003).

blockers: No schedule, result or shot source is wired; prices are not captured; league coverage is undefined.
enable: Choose leagues, wire a licensed results/xG source, build the Dixon-Coles brain on the hockey harness, validate, then authorise capture.

sports.label: Tennis (ATP/WTA)

brain.approach: Existing: a regularised logistic model on overall and surface Elo, ranking and form. Designed extension: serve/return point probabilities combined into match probabilities (barnett2005, klaassen2003).
brain.why: Elo-type ratings are the strongest published pre-match predictors (kovalchik2016); serve/return models add surface and format structure.

sports.label: UFC / MMA

brain.approach: Designed: opponent-adjusted per-minute rates (significant strikes landed/absorbed, takedowns, control time, submission attempts) driving a Markov chain of fight states → win, method (KO/TKO, submission, decision) and round probabilities, with a Glicko rating as the baseline.
brain.why: Holmes, McHale & Zychaluk (2023) show a Markov chain on in-fight statistics matches bookmaker accuracy; rating systems (glickman1999) are the simple baseline.
not_modelled: everything priced: the only probability today is the market's de-vigged one

blockers: No independent model; no per-minute fight statistics archive is wired.
enable: Wire a fight-statistics archive, build the Markov brain, validate walk-forward against outcomes and the close.
